content.question: Your nightly test run shows "47 tests failed." Your manager asks "What broke?" You open the report and see... just red X marks. No logs, no request/response bodies, no context. How long until you find the bug?
content.code:
❌ testCreateUser - AssertionError: expected 201 but got 500
// Cool. But WHY did it return 500? What was the request body?

content.prompt: Add logging to capture the FULL request and response when a test fails.
content.hint: RestAssured has `.log().all()` and Allure has `@Step` annotations.
content.expectedOutput: Full request/response visible in failure reports

content.text: A test report without context is like a doctor saying "you're sick" without running tests. Allure reports are like a complete medical chart — symptoms (assertion failure), history (request sent), lab results (response received), and diagnosis (root cause). Good reporting means ANY team member can diagnose a failure without re-running the test or asking you.

content.annotation: `AllureRestAssured()` filter automatically captures request/response in Allure reports. `addAttachment` lets you attach extra context — response bodies, screenshots, environment info. When this test fails, the Allure report shows EXACTLY what was sent and received.

content.modification: Tests run in CI with 50 parallel threads. Where do these logs GO?
content.question: What's wrong with `.log().all()` in CI?
options: Console logs get interleaved and unreadable
content.explanation: With parallel execution, console logs from 50 threads mix together — you can't tell which request belongs to which test. Use structured logging (Allure attachments, test listeners) that attach logs PER TEST instead of dumping to shared console output.

content.label: Allure Reports vs ExtentReports
content.question: Which is better for a large SDET team?
options: Allure - less boilerplate and CI plugins
content.explanation: Allure uses `@Step` annotations and the `AllureRestAssured()` filter to capture request/response automatically with minimal code. It attaches context via `addAttachment` and integrates with CI out of the box. ExtentReports requires programmatic logging for every action. For large teams, Allure's annotation-driven approach means less boilerplate and consistent reporting across all test classes.

content.prompt: How do you debug a test that passed yesterday and failed today with no code change?
content.sentence: I check the _____ report which shows the exact request body and full response received, the environment state, and the _____ tab showing when it last passed — common causes include test data pollution from _____ runs.

content.text: At Amazon, test reports are reviewed daily in operational dashboards:
content.code:
Test Suite: UserService API
Pass Rate: 98.2% (196/200)
Failed: testRateLimit (timeout), testBulkCreate (500)
Trend: ↓ from 99.5% since Tuesday
Action: Rate limit test needs longer timeout for gamma
content.note: As an SDET-1, your test reports are a SERVICE HEALTH SIGNAL. When tests fail, on-call engineers read YOUR reports to decide if it's a test issue or a real service bug. Clear reporting with request/response context saves hours of debugging during incidents.
